passages.original: omnes acclamarunt gratias se inter cetera etiam ob hoc agere, quod admoniti essent, ut tam pio, tam necessario officio fungerentur. ingens numerus erat bello Punico captorum, quos Hannibal, cum ab suis non redimerentur, venum dederat. multitudinis eorum argumentum est, quod Polybius scribit centum talentis eam rem Achaeis stetisse, cum quingenos denarios pretium in capita, quod redderetur dominis, statuissent. mille enim ducentos ea ratione Achaia habuit. adice nunc pro portione, quot verisimile sit Graeciam totam habuisse.
passages.english: All cried out that, among other things, they also gave thanks for this, that they had been reminded to perform so dutiful and so necessary an obligation. There was a huge number of men captured in the Punic War whom Hannibal, since they were not being ransomed by their own people, had sold into slavery. Proof of their great number is what Polybius writes, that this business cost the Achaeans a hundred talents, although they had fixed the price to be paid back to the owners at five hundred denarii a head. For on that reckoning Achaia held one thousand two hundred [of them]. Add now, in proportion, how many it is likely that all Greece held.
